instruction:
Task background: After a recent merge, the internal Acme Catalog landing page saw its Lighthouse performance score drop from ~92 to ~35, with TBT jumping from ~150 ms to ~1800 ms+. CI only emits Lighthouse JSON numbers and cannot tell you which piece of code or which resource caused the long tasks, blocked rendering, or shipped a large amount of never-executed bytes. You need to locate ≥ 2 root causes, produce a minimal fix, and prove the improvement by re-running and comparing the numbers.

Ready-to-use materials on the box:
- Page under test: `http://localhost:7100/` (warmup brings it up automatically).
- Same-origin smoke entry `http://localhost:7100/?optimized=1` is provided for comparison observation only — **it is not the answer**; do not submit it as a deliverable (a SHA-256 comparison is performed).
- Application source: `/tmp_workspace/app/` (i.e. `exec/`), containing `public/index.html`, `public/js/blockerA.js`, `public/js/legacy-bundle.js`, `public/js/tracker.js`, etc. Warmup leaves a ready-to-use `serve_optimized.js` helper that can expose `/tmp_workspace/results/index.optimized.html` on port 7101.

Goal: identify which resources are the root cause of the regression, write a fixed HTML, deploy it on a separate port so Lighthouse can re-run and compare, and leave behind complete evidence that a third party can audit. How to gather evidence, how to drive the browser, and which tools to use (Lighthouse / browser DevTools panels / any CDP client / source analysis / etc.) is up to you.

You must produce the following deliverables under `/tmp_workspace/results/`:

1. **Lighthouse raw JSON (before / after)**
   - `lh_before.json`: full Lighthouse JSON from running the performance category against the page under test `http://localhost:7100/`. Must contain the `audits` and `categories.performance` fields.
   - `lh_after.json`: JSON from running the same audit against your fixed page deployed on port 7101.

2. **Numeric summary (before / after)**
   - `lh_summary_before.json` / `lh_summary_after.json`: a distilled summary extracted from the corresponding Lighthouse JSON, containing at least `categories.performance.score`, `audits.total-blocking-time.numericValue`, `audits.largest-contentful-paint.numericValue`, `audits.render-blocking-resources.details.items[*].url`, and `audits.unused-javascript.details.items[*]`.

3. **Root-cause list**
   - `root_causes.json`, schema:
     ```json
     {
       "culprits": [
         {"file": "<basename>", "kind": "<render-blocking|unused-bytes|long-task-after-dcl|...>",
          "evidence_ms": <int optional>, "evidence_kb": <int optional>,
          "screenshot": "<view_*.png filename>"}
       ]
     }
     ```
     At least 2 entries; each `file` must be the trailing segment of a resource that actually appears in `lh_summary_before.json`; at least 2 entries must reference an actual screenshot from the next item via the `screenshot` field.

4. **Coverage evidence**
   - `coverage_before.json`: JS coverage data collected against the page under test (organized by file/range is fine). The file must be ≥ 200 bytes and must actually contain at least one resource trailing segment from the root-cause list (e.g. `legacy-bundle.js`). Lighthouse's `unused-javascript` audit only gives ratios, not absolute unused bytes per file, so this data must be collected independently and cannot be derived directly from `lh_before.json`.

5. **Fixed HTML**
   - `index.optimized.html`: the fixed HTML file you produce. Hard constraints:
     - Its SHA-256 must **differ** from `/tmp_workspace/app/public/index.ok.html` (you may not directly copy the smoke file);
     - It must **no longer** contain a synchronous `<script src="…blockerA.js">` (it must be removed or annotated with `async`/`defer`/`type="module"`);
     - If it still references `legacy-bundle.js`, the corresponding `<script>` must carry one of `async` / `defer` / `type="module"`;
     - If it still references `tracker.js`, the corresponding `<script>` must carry one of `async` / `defer` / `type="module"` (or be dynamically injected at an idle moment such as `requestIdleCallback`).

6. **Servable endpoint for the fixed version**
   - An HTTP service listening on `127.0.0.1:7101` that on `GET /` returns 200 plus the real HTML text of the `index.optimized.html` above (**not** a 302 / redirect back to `:7100/?optimized=1`). Warmup leaves a `serve_optimized.js` template that can be reused or replaced directly.
   - `serve_optimized.log`: the run log of that service (any text is fine; for human review).

7. **Visual evidence screenshots** (each ≥ 4 KB, from real rendered state — not fabricated text)
   - `view_perf_flamechart_long_task.png`: a flame chart in the browser DevTools Performance view that shows a ≥ 1 s "Evaluate Script" long task, with an overlay tooltip on that task exposing the root-cause JS filename and self time (this combination of data is **not** in the raw trace JSON and must come from the rendered state).
   - `view_perf_bottom_up.png`: the Bottom-Up view (sorted by Self Time) from the same recording, with at least 5 rows showing a `Self Time` column and file links (e.g. `*.js:<line>`).
   - `view_coverage_panel.png`: the Coverage view, showing at least one root-cause JS row (e.g. `legacy-bundle.js`) with its Unused Bytes number and the red/blue usage visualization bar; that number must be ≥ 400 KB scale.
   - `view_perf_after.png`: a flame chart screenshot from doing the same performance recording against the fixed endpoint (port 7101), visibly narrower than before and no longer containing a ≥ 1 s "Evaluate Script" long task.

8. **Final report**
   - `findings.json`, must contain all of the following keys:
     ```json
     {
       "tbt_before_ms": <float>,
       "tbt_after_ms": <float>,
       "lcp_before_ms": <float>,
       "lcp_after_ms": <float>,
       "perf_score_before": <0..1>,
       "perf_score_after": <0..1>,
       "tbt_improvement_ratio": <float>,
       "fixes_applied": ["<human-readable fix entry>", ...],
       "evidence_screenshots": [
         "view_perf_flamechart_long_task.png",
         "view_perf_bottom_up.png",
         "view_coverage_panel.png",
         "view_perf_after.png"
       ]
     }
     ```
     The `tbt_*` / `lcp_*` / `perf_score_*` values must agree with `lh_before.json` / `lh_after.json` within ±15%.

Hard constraints:
- In `lh_after.json`, `categories.performance.score` ≥ 0.70; `(tbt_before − tbt_after) / tbt_before ≥ 0.40`.
- In `lh_after.json`, `largest-contentful-paint.numericValue` ≤ 3500 ms.
- All numeric values must come from real Lighthouse runs and real coverage collection — fabrication or direct copying from the smoke entry is not allowed.

parameters.warmup:
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/state /opt/web10_gt && chmod 777 /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/state
if [ -f /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json ]; then
  mv /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json /opt/web10_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || cp /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json /opt/web10_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || true
  chown -R root:root /opt/web10_gt 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 700 /opt/web10_gt 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 600 /opt/web10_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf /tmp_workspace/gt 2>/dev/null || true
fi
which curl || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing curl ca-certificates && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which jq || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing jq && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which node || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing nodejs npm && break; sleep 5; done) || true
pip3 install --break-system-packages --quiet playwright 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --quiet playwright || true
PWB="chro""mium"
python3 -m playwright install "$PWB" >/tmp/pw_install.log 2>&1 || true
export CHROME_PATH="$(ls -1 /root/.cache/ms-playwright/${PWB}-*/chrome-linux/chrome 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
[ -n "$CHROME_PATH" ] && ln -sf "$CHROME_PATH" /usr/local/bin/chrome || true
which tesseract || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing tesseract-ocr fonts-noto-cjk poppler-utils && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which lighthouse || timeout 300 npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit --silent lighthouse@11.7.1 || true
pip3 install --break-system-packages --ignore-installed --quiet blinker 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --ignore-installed --quiet blinker || true
pip3 install --break-system-packages --quiet pillow pytesseract requests 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --quiet pillow pytesseract requests || true
cd /tmp_workspace && timeout 240 npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund express@4.19.2 chrome-launcher@1.1.0 || true
cd /tmp_workspace && node build_legacy_bundle.js >/tmp/build_bundle.log 2>&1 || true
cd /tmp_workspace && nohup node server.js >/tmp/start.log 2>&1 & sleep 3; for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -sf http://localhost:7100/healthz >/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done

evaluator.desc: Run the WeaveBench rule-based grade() inside the VM and parse its REWARD score.
